questions.text: किसी पतली प्लास्टिक की छड़ को त्रिज्या R के वृत्ताकार वलय के रूप में मोड़ा गया है। इसे आवेश घनत्व λ से एकसमान आवेशित किया गया है। इसके केन्द्र पर विद्युत-क्षेत्र का परिमाण है :
questions.text_english: A thin plastic rod is bent into a circular ring of radius R. It is uniformly charged with charge density λ. The magnitude of the electric field at its centre is :
questions.solution: The correct answer is (B) Zero. A uniformly charged circular ring has a symmetric charge distribution. The electric field contributions from diametrically opposite elements are equal in magnitude but opposite in direction. Therefore, all horizontal and vertical components cancel out, making the net electric field at the centre exactly zero. Options A, C, and D are incorrect because they suggest a non-zero field, which would violate the symmetry of the charge distribution.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (B) शून्य है। एकसमान आवेशित वृत्ताकार वलय में सममित आवेश वितरण होता है। व्यासीय रूप से विपरीत अवयवों के विद्युत-क्षेत्र योगदान परिमाण में बराबर लेकिन दिशा में विपरीत होते हैं, इसलिए केन्द्र पर कुल विद्युत-क्षेत्र शून्य होता है।
questions.topic: Electric field due to a uniformly charged ring

questions.text: तीन आवेशित छोटे गोले X, Y और Z जिन पर क्रमशः आवेश +q, –q और +q हैं, आरेख में दर्शाए अनुसार एक-दूसरे से समदूरस्थ स्थित हैं। गोले Y और Z को स्थिर रखा गया है। आरम्भ में X भी अपने स्थान पर स्थिर है परन्तु यह गति के लिए स्वतंत्र है। जब X को मुक्त किया जाता है, तो इसके द्वारा चला गया पथ होगा :
questions.text_english: Three small charged spheres X, Y and Z carrying charges +q, –q and +q respectively are placed equidistant from each other, as shown in the figure. The spheres Y and Z are held in place. Initially X is also held in place, but is otherwise free to move. When X is released, the path followed by it will be :
questions.solution: The correct answer is (C). Sphere X carries +q charge. Y carries –q (attracts X) and Z carries +q (repels X). The net force on X is a combination of attraction toward Y and repulsion from Z. Since Y is below-left and Z is to the right of X, the attractive force toward Y and repulsive force from Z result in a net force that curves X toward path C, which bends toward the right and downward in the direction of Y. Paths A, B, and D do not represent the correct resultant direction of the net electrostatic force on X.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (C) है। X पर +q आवेश है। Y (−q) X को आकर्षित करता है और Z (+q) X को प्रतिकर्षित करता है। दोनों बलों के परिणामी की दिशा पथ C के अनुसार होती है।
questions.topic: Coulomb's law and superposition of forces

questions.text: किसी एकसमान सीधे तार में, चालन इलेक्ट्रॉन +x दिशा के अनुदिश गमन करते हैं। मान लीजिए तार में E→ और j→ क्रमशः विद्युत-क्षेत्र और धारा घनत्व हैं। तब :
questions.text_english: In a uniform straight wire, conduction electrons move along +x direction. Let E and j be the electric field and current density in the wire, respectively. Then :

options.A: E→ और j→ दोनों +x दिशा के अनुदिश हैं।
options.B: E→ और j→ दोनों –x दिशा के अनुदिश हैं।
options.C: E→ +x दिशा के अनुदिश, परन्तु j→ –x दिशा के अनुदिश है।
options.D: E→ –x दिशा के अनुदिश, परन्तु j→ +x दिशा के अनुदिश है।

options_english.A: E and j both are along +x direction.
options_english.B: E and j both are along –x direction.
options_english.C: E is along +x direction, but j is along –x direction.
options_english.D: E is along –x direction, but j is along +x direction.

questions.solution: The correct answer is (A). Electrons carry negative charge and move in the +x direction. Conventional current flows opposite to the motion of electrons, i.e., in the –x direction? No — wait: if electrons move in +x, conventional current j flows in the –x direction. However, the electric field E drives electrons and must point opposite to the electron motion, so E points in the –x direction. Current density j is in the direction of conventional current, i.e., –x. Therefore both E and j are along –x. The correct answer is (B). Both E and j are along –x direction because electrons moving in +x means conventional current is in –x, and E must also be in –x to push electrons in +x (since force on electron = –eE, and force is in +x, E must be in –x).
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (B) है। इलेक्ट्रॉन +x दिशा में गति करते हैं, अतः पारंपरिक धारा −x दिशा में है। विद्युत-क्षेत्र E→ भी −x दिशा में होगा क्योंकि इलेक्ट्रॉन पर बल F = −eE होता है, और बल +x दिशा में होने के लिए E का −x दिशा में होना आवश्यक है। इसलिए E→ और j→ दोनों −x दिशा में हैं।
questions.topic: Current density and electric field in a conductor

questions.text: दो आवेशित कणों P और Q जिन पर समान आवेश q परन्तु जिनके द्रव्यमान m₁ और m₂ हैं, को समान विभवान्तर V द्वारा त्वरित किया गया है। ये चुम्बकीय क्षेत्र B (⊥v→) के प्रदेश में प्रवेश करने पर क्रमशः a और b त्रिज्याओं के वृत्ताकार पथ पर गति करते हैं। तब (m₁/m₂) बराबर है
questions.text_english: Two charged particles, P and Q, each having charge q but of masses m₁ and m₂, are accelerated through the same potential difference V. They enter a region of magnetic field B (⊥v) and describe the circular paths of radii a and b respectively. Then (m₁/m₂) is equal to :
questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) (a/b)². When a charge q is accelerated through potential difference V, its kinetic energy is qV = ½mv². In a magnetic field B, the radius of circular motion is r = mv/(qB). So r = (1/qB)√(2mqV). Thus r ∝ √m, giving r₁/r₂ = √(m₁/m₂), i.e., a/b = √(m₁/m₂), therefore m₁/m₂ = (a/b)². Options A, B, and D do not follow correctly from the relationship between radius and mass in a magnetic field.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (C) है। विभवान्तर V से त्वरित आवेश q के लिए: r = (1/qB)√(2mqV), अतः r ∝ √m। इसलिए a/b = √(m₁/m₂), जिससे m₁/m₂ = (a/b)² प्राप्त होता है।
questions.topic: Circular motion of charged particle in magnetic field

questions.text: प्रतिरोध G के किसी गैल्वेनोमीटर को 0 से I A परास के ऐमीटर में परिवर्तित किया गया है। यदि इस गैल्वेनोमीटर में प्रवाहित धारा I A की 0·1% है, तो ऐमीटर का प्रतिरोध है :
questions.text_english: A galvanometer of resistance G is converted into an ammeter of range 0 to I A. If the current through the galvanometer is 0.1% of I A, the resistance of the ammeter is :
questions.solution: The correct answer is (A) G/999. The galvanometer carries 0.1% of I A, so Ig = 0.001I. The shunt resistance S is connected in parallel with the galvanometer. Using the relation Ig·G = (I – Ig)·S: 0.001I × G = (I – 0.001I) × S = 0.999I × S, giving S = G/999. The ammeter resistance = GS/(G+S) ≈ S = G/999 (since S << G). Therefore the resistance of the ammeter is G/999.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (A) G/999 है। गैल्वेनोमीटर में प्रवाहित धारा Ig = 0.001I है। शंट प्रतिरोध S के लिए: Ig·G = (I–Ig)·S, से S = G/999 प्राप्त होता है।
questions.topic: Conversion of galvanometer to ammeter

questions.text: कोई 10 cm लम्बा तार y-अक्ष के अनुदिश रखा है। इससे धनात्मक y-दिशा में 1.0 A की धारा प्रवाहित हो रही है। इस क्षेत्र में कोई चुम्बकीय क्षेत्र B = (5 mT)ĵ + (8 mT)k̂ विद्यमान है। इस तार पर बल है :
questions.text_english: A 10 cm long wire lies along y-axis. It carries a current of 1.0 A in positive y-direction. A magnetic field B = (5 mT)ĵ + (8 mT)k̂ exists in the region. The force on the wire is :
questions.solution: The correct answer is (A) (0·8 mN)î. The force on a current-carrying wire is F = IL × B. Here, IL = (1.0 A)(0.10 m)ĵ = 0.1 ĵ A·m. B = (5 mT)ĵ + (8 mT)k̂. F = 0.1ĵ × [(5×10⁻³)ĵ + (8×10⁻³)k̂] = 0.1 × 5×10⁻³ (ĵ×ĵ) + 0.1 × 8×10⁻³ (ĵ×k̂) = 0 + 0.1 × 8×10⁻³ î = 8×10⁻⁴ N î = 0.8 mN î. Therefore the force is (0.8 mN)î.
questions.topic: Force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field

questions.text: किसी ट्रांसफॉर्मर की प्राथमिक और द्वितीयक कुण्डलियों में फेरों की संख्या क्रमशः 500 और 5000 है। प्राथमिक कुण्डली 220 V 50 Hz के ac स्रोत से संयोजित है। द्वितीयक कुण्डली के सिरों पर निर्गत है :
questions.text_english: The primary and secondary coils of a transformer have 500 turns and 5000 turns respectively. The primary coil is connected to an ac source of 220 V 50 Hz. The output across the secondary coil is :
questions.solution: The correct answer is (D) 2200 V 50 Hz. For a transformer, Vs/Vp = Ns/Np. Here Ns/Np = 5000/500 = 10. Therefore Vs = 10 × 220 V = 2200 V. The frequency of the output remains the same as the input frequency, i.e., 50 Hz. A transformer only changes voltage, not frequency. Option C is incorrect because the frequency does not change to 5 Hz.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (D) है। Vs = (Ns/Np) × Vp = (5000/500) × 220 = 2200 V। आवृत्ति अपरिवर्तित रहती है, अतः निर्गत 2200 V, 50 Hz है।
questions.topic: Transformer: turns ratio and voltage transformation

questions.text: निम्नलिखित में से उस वैज्ञानिक को पहचानिए, जिन्होंने सर्वप्रथम 25 mm – 5 mm परास की तरंगदैर्घ्यों की विद्युत-चुम्बकीय तरंगों को उत्पन्न करके उनका प्रेक्षण किया था :
questions.text_english: The first scientist who produced and observed electromagnetic waves of wavelengths in the range 25 mm – 5 mm was :
questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) J.C. Bose. Jagadish Chandra Bose was the first scientist to produce and detect electromagnetic waves in the microwave range of wavelengths 5 mm to 25 mm. Maxwell theoretically predicted electromagnetic waves but did not produce them experimentally. Hertz produced radio waves of much longer wavelength. Marconi worked on long-distance radio communication.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (C) J.C. Bose है। जगदीश चंद्र बोस ने सर्वप्रथम 5 mm से 25 mm तरंगदैर्ध्य परास की विद्युत-चुम्बकीय (माइक्रोवेव) तरंगों का उत्पादन और प्रेक्षण किया।
questions.topic: History of electromagnetic waves and their discoverers

questions.text: किसी गतिमान इलेक्ट्रॉन और किसी गतिमान प्रोटॉन से सम्बद्ध तरंगों का तरंगदैर्घ्य समान λ है। इसका यह अभिप्राय है कि इनका/इनकी समान है :
questions.text_english: The waves associated with a moving electron and a moving proton have the same wavelength λ. It implies that they have the same :
questions.solution: The correct answer is (A) momentum. According to de Broglie's hypothesis, the wavelength associated with a particle is λ = h/p, where p is the linear momentum. If two particles have the same de Broglie wavelength λ, they must have the same momentum p = h/λ, regardless of their masses. Speed, energy, and angular momentum can differ between an electron and a proton with the same wavelength since they have different masses.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (A) संवेग है। दे ब्रॉग्ली के अनुसार λ = h/p। यदि दोनों का λ समान है, तो p = h/λ भी समान होगा, चाहे उनके द्रव्यमान भिन्न हों।
questions.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.topic: de Broglie wavelength and momentum

questions.text: दो पुंज, A और B जिनके फोटॉनों की ऊर्जा क्रमशः 3·3 eV और 11·3 eV हैं, क्रमवार किसी धात्विक पृष्ठ (कार्य-फलन 2·3 eV) को प्रदीप्त करते हैं। पुंज A के कारण उत्सर्जित इलेक्ट्रॉनों की अधिकतम चाल का पुंज B से अनुपात है :
questions.text_english: Two beams, A and B whose photon energies are 3·3 eV and 11·3 eV respectively, illuminate a metallic surface (work function 2·3 eV) successively. The ratio of maximum speed of electrons emitted due to beam A to that due to beam B is :
questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) 1/3. The maximum kinetic energy of emitted electrons is KE = hν – φ. For beam A: KE_A = 3.3 – 2.3 = 1.0 eV. For beam B: KE_B = 11.3 – 2.3 = 9.0 eV. Since KE = ½mv², we have v ∝ √(KE). Therefore v_A/v_B = √(KE_A/KE_B) = √(1/9) = 1/3. The ratio of maximum speeds is 1/3.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (C) 1/3 है। KE_A = 1.0 eV, KE_B = 9.0 eV। v ∝ √KE, अतः v_A/v_B = √(1/9) = 1/3।
questions.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.topic: Photoelectric effect: maximum kinetic energy and speed of photoelectrons

questions.text: हाइड्रोजन परमाणु के स्पेक्ट्रम में बामर श्रेणी की दूसरी स्पेक्ट्रमी रेखा के निर्माण को उत्पन्न करने वाला इलेक्ट्रॉन का संक्रमण संगत होता है :
questions.text_english: The transition of electron that gives rise to the formation of the second spectral line of the Balmer series in the spectrum of hydrogen atom corresponds to :
questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) nf = 2 and ni = 4. The Balmer series corresponds to transitions where the final state is nf = 2. The first line corresponds to the transition ni = 3 → nf = 2. The second spectral line corresponds to the next transition, which is ni = 4 → nf = 2. Therefore, the second line of the Balmer series arises from the transition ni = 4 to nf = 2.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (C) है। बामर श्रेणी में nf = 2 होता है। पहली रेखा ni = 3 से और दूसरी रेखा ni = 4 से आती है, अतः nf = 2 और ni = 4।
questions.topic: Hydrogen spectrum: Balmer series transitions

questions.text: Ge का मादन As के साथ किया गया है। इसके कारण :
questions.text_english: Ge is doped with As. Due to doping,

options.A: Ge के जालक की संरचना विकृत हो जाती है।
options.B: चालन इलेक्ट्रॉनों की संख्या में वृद्धि होती है।
options.C: होलों की संख्या में वृद्धि होती है।
options.D: चालन इलेक्ट्रॉनों की संख्या में कमी होती है।

options_english.A: the structure of Ge lattice is distorted.
options_english.B: the number of conduction electrons increases.
options_english.D: the number of conduction electrons decreases.

questions.solution: The correct answer is (B). Arsenic (As) is a pentavalent impurity (donor impurity). When As is doped into Germanium (Ge), each As atom contributes one extra free electron to the crystal. This creates an n-type semiconductor where the number of conduction electrons increases significantly. The lattice structure is not distorted because As atoms replace Ge atoms in the lattice. Holes do not increase because As is a donor, not an acceptor.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (B) है। As एक पंचसंयोजी दाता अशुद्धि है। Ge में As मिलाने से प्रत्येक As परमाणु एक अतिरिक्त मुक्त इलेक्ट्रॉन प्रदान करता है, जिससे n-प्रकार का अर्धचालक बनता है और चालन इलेक्ट्रॉनों की संख्या बढ़ती है।
questions.topic: Doping of semiconductors: n-type

questions.text:
अभिकथन (A) : किसी बैटरी से श्रेणी में संयोजित और स्वतंत्रतापूर्वक निलम्बित दो लम्बे समान्तर तार एक-दूसरे से दूर हटते हैं।
कारण (R) : विपरीत दिशाओं में प्रवाहित धारावाही दो तार एक-दूसरे को प्रतिकर्षित करते हैं।
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A): Two long parallel wires, freely suspended and connected in series to a battery, move apart.
Reason (R): Two wires carrying current in opposite directions repel each other.
questions.instruction_line: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) प्रकार के प्रश्न। नीचे दिए गए कूट (A), (B), (C) और (D) में से सही उत्तर चुनिए।
questions.instruction_line_english: Assertion (A) and Reason (R) type question. Select the correct answer from codes (A), (B), (C) and (D).

options.A: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं और कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता है।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) सही है, परन्तु कारण (R) गलत है।
options.D: अभिकथन (A) गलत है तथा कारण (R) भी गलत है।

options_english.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
options_english.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
options_english.D: Assertion (A) is false and Reason (R) is also false.

questions.solution: The correct answer is (A). When two wires are connected in series to a battery and suspended freely, current flows through them in opposite directions (since one end of each wire connects to each other and the battery terminals are at the far ends). Two parallel wires carrying currents in opposite directions repel each other. Both the assertion and the reason are true, and the reason correctly explains why the wires move apart.
questions.solution_hindi: सही उत्तर (A) है। श्रेणी संयोजन में दोनों तारों में धारा विपरीत दिशाओं में प्रवाहित होती है। विपरीत दिशाओं में धारावाही तार प्रतिकर्षित होते हैं, इसलिए वे दूर हटते हैं। अभिकथन और कारण दोनों सही हैं और कारण सही व्याख्या करता है।
questions.topic: Force between two parallel current-carrying wires

questions.text:
अभिकथन (A) : समतल दर्पण और उत्तल दर्पण किसी भी परिस्थिति में वास्तविक प्रतिबिम्ब नहीं बना सकते हैं।
कारण (R) : कोई आभासी प्रतिबिम्ब वास्तविक प्रतिबिम्ब बनाने के लिए बिम्ब की भाँति कार्य नहीं कर सकता है।
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A): Plane and convex mirrors cannot produce real images under any circumstance.
Reason (R): A virtual image cannot serve as an object to produce a real image.

questions.solution: The correct answer is (C). The Assertion is true: plane and convex mirrors always form virtual, erect, and diminished (or same-size) images and cannot produce real images on their own. However, the Reason is false: a virtual image can indeed serve as a virtual object for another optical system to produce a real image. For example, if convergent rays fall on a plane mirror (being converged by a lens), a real image can be formed. Therefore Assertion is true but the Reason is false.

Assertion (A): The mutual inductance between two coils is maximum when the coils are wound on each other.
Reason (R): The flux linkage between two coils is maximum when they are wound on each other.

options.A: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं और कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता है।

questions.solution: The correct answer is (A). Mutual inductance M = Nφ/I and depends on the flux linkage between two coils. When two coils are wound on each other (bifilar winding), the flux produced by one coil links completely with the other coil, making the flux linkage maximum. Since M is directly proportional to flux linkage, mutual inductance is also maximum. Both statements are true and the Reason correctly explains the Assertion.

questions.text_english:
Assertion (A): In photoelectric effect, the kinetic energy of the emitted photoelectrons increases with increase in the intensity of the incident light.
Reason (R): Photoelectric current depends on the wavelength of the incident light.

options.A: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं और कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता है।

options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation.
options_english.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.

questions.solution: The correct answer is (D). The Assertion is false: the kinetic energy of photoelectrons depends on the frequency (not intensity) of incident light. Increasing intensity only increases the number of emitted electrons (photoelectric current), not their kinetic energy. The Reason is also false: photoelectric current depends on the intensity of light, not its wavelength. Wavelength (or frequency) determines whether emission occurs and the maximum kinetic energy of emitted electrons.

questions.text: लम्बाई L और अनुप्रस्थ-काट क्षेत्रफल A के किसी एकसमान तार का प्रतिरोध R है। इस तार को एकसमान रूप से खींचकर इसकी लम्बाई में 25% वृद्धि की गई है। तार के प्रतिरोध में प्रतिशत वृद्धि परिकलित कीजिए।
questions.text_english: A uniform wire of length L and area of cross-section A has resistance R. The wire is uniformly stretched so that its length increases by 25%. Calculate the percentage increase in the resistance of the wire.

key_points: New length L' = 1.25L; volume is conserved so new area A' = A/1.25 = 0.8A
New resistance R' = ρL'/A' = ρ(1.25L)/(0.8A) = 1.5625R
Percentage increase = (R' – R)/R × 100 = 56.25%

questions.solution: When the wire is stretched, its volume remains constant: V = LA = L'A'. New length L' = 1.25L. Therefore A' = LA/L' = LA/(1.25L) = A/1.25 = 0.8A. Resistance R = ρL/A, so new resistance R' = ρL'/A' = ρ(1.25L)/(0.8A) = (1.25/0.8)R = 1.5625R. Percentage increase in resistance = [(R' – R)/R] × 100 = [(1.5625R – R)/R] × 100 = 0.5625 × 100 = 56.25%.
questions.solution_hindi: आयतन स्थिर रहता है: LA = L'A'। L' = 1.25L, अतः A' = 0.8A। नया प्रतिरोध R' = ρL'/A' = 1.5625R। प्रतिरोध में प्रतिशत वृद्धि = 56.25%।
questions.topic: Resistivity and effect of stretching on resistance

questions.text: कोई बिम्ब 40 cm वक्रता त्रिज्या के किसी अवतल दर्पण के सामने 30 cm दूरी पर स्थित है। (i) बने प्रतिबिम्ब की स्थिति तथा (ii) प्रतिबिम्ब का आवर्धन ज्ञात कीजिए।
questions.text_english: An object is placed 30 cm in front of a concave mirror of radius of curvature 40 cm. Find the (i) position of the image formed and (ii) magnification of the image.

key_points: Focal length f = R/2 = 40/2 = –20 cm (concave mirror)
Using mirror formula: 1/v + 1/u = 1/f; u = –30 cm; 1/v = 1/f – 1/u = –1/20 + 1/30 = –1/60; v = –60 cm
Magnification m = –v/u = –(–60)/(–30) = –2

questions.solution: For a concave mirror, focal length f = –R/2 = –40/2 = –20 cm. Object distance u = –30 cm. Using the mirror formula 1/v + 1/u = 1/f: 1/v = 1/f – 1/u = 1/(–20) – 1/(–30) = –1/20 + 1/30 = (–3+2)/60 = –1/60. Therefore v = –60 cm. The image is formed 60 cm in front of the mirror (real and inverted). Magnification m = –v/u = –(–60)/(–30) = –2. The image is real, inverted, and magnified twice the size of the object.
questions.solution_hindi: (i) f = –20 cm, u = –30 cm। दर्पण सूत्र से v = –60 cm। प्रतिबिम्ब दर्पण के सामने 60 cm पर बनता है। (ii) m = –v/u = –2। प्रतिबिम्ब वास्तविक, उलटा और 2 गुना बड़ा है।
questions.topic: Concave mirror: image position and magnification

questions.text: गतिज ऊर्जा E के किसी न्यूट्रॉन (द्रव्यमान m) तथा समान ऊर्जा के किसी फोटॉन पर विचार कीजिए। मान लीजिए न्यूट्रॉन की दे ब्रॉग्ली तरंगदैर्ध्य λn तथा फोटॉन की तरंगदैर्ध्य λp है। λn/λp के लिए व्यंजक प्राप्त कीजिए।
questions.text_english: Consider a neutron (mass m) of kinetic energy E and a photon of the same energy. Let λn and λp be the de Broglie wavelength of neutron and the wavelength of photon respectively. Obtain an expression for λn/λp.

key_points: For neutron: λn = h/p = h/√(2mE)
For photon: λp = hc/E

questions.solution: For the neutron of kinetic energy E and mass m: momentum p = √(2mE), so de Broglie wavelength λn = h/p = h/√(2mE). For the photon of energy E: wavelength λp = hc/E. Therefore, λn/λp = [h/√(2mE)] ÷ [hc/E] = [h/√(2mE)] × [E/(hc)] = E/(c√(2mE)) = √E/(c√(2m)) = √(E/2mc²). This is the required expression for λn/λp.
questions.solution_hindi: न्यूट्रॉन के लिए: λn = h/√(2mE)। फोटॉन के लिए: λp = hc/E। अतः λn/λp = E/(c√(2mE)) = √(E/(2mc²))।
questions.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.topic: de Broglie wavelength comparison of neutron and photon

questions.text:
(क) आवृत्ति 5·0 × 10¹⁴ Hz का एकवर्णी प्रकाश वायु से अपवर्तनांक 1·5 वाले माध्यम में गमन करता है। दोनों माध्यमों के अन्तरापृष्ठ पर (i) परावर्तित प्रकाश, तथा (ii) अपवर्तित प्रकाश की तरंगदैर्घ्य ज्ञात कीजिए।
अथवा
(ख) 16 cm फोकस दूरी का कोई समतलोत्तल लेंस अपवर्तनांक 1·4 के पदार्थ का बना है। लेंस के वक्रित पृष्ठ की त्रिज्या परिकलित कीजिए।
questions.text_english:
(a) Monochromatic light of frequency 5·0 × 10¹⁴ Hz passes from air into a medium of refractive index 1·5. Find the wavelength of the light (i) reflected, and (ii) refracted at the interface of the two media.
OR
(b) A plano-convex lens of focal length 16 cm is made of a material of refractive index 1·4. Calculate the radius of the curved surface of the lens.

key_points: (a)(i) Reflected light wavelength: λ = c/f = (3×10⁸)/(5×10¹⁴) = 6×10⁻⁷ m = 600 nm (wavelength in air, unchanged)
(a)(ii) Refracted light wavelength: λ' = λ/n = 600/1.5 = 400 nm

questions.solution:
Part (a): The frequency of light does not change at any interface. For reflected light, it remains in air, so wavelength λ_reflected = c/f = (3×10⁸)/(5×10¹⁴) = 6×10⁻⁷ m = 600 nm. For refracted light entering a medium of refractive index n = 1.5, wavelength λ_refracted = λ/n = 600/1.5 = 400 nm.

Part (b) OR: For a plano-convex lens, one surface is flat (R₂ = ∞) and one is curved (R₁ = R). Using the lens maker's formula: 1/f = (n–1)[1/R₁ – 1/R₂] = (1.4–1)(1/R – 0) = 0.4/R. Given f = 16 cm: 1/16 = 0.4/R, so R = 0.4 × 16 = 6.4 cm.
questions.solution_hindi:
(क) परावर्तित प्रकाश की λ = 600 nm (वायु में अपरिवर्तित)। अपवर्तित प्रकाश की λ' = 600/1.5 = 400 nm।
(ख) लेंस निर्माता सूत्र से: 1/16 = (1.4–1)/R; R = 6.4 cm।
questions.topic: Refraction: wavelength change and lens maker's formula

questions.text: विसरण धारा तथा अपवाह धारा में अन्तर बताइए। p-n संधि निर्माण में इनकी भूमिका समझाइए।
questions.text_english: Differentiate between diffusion current and drift current. Explain their role in the formation of p-n junction.

key_points: Diffusion current: due to concentration gradient of charge carriers (holes from p to n, electrons from n to p); no external field needed
Drift current: due to electric field across the depletion region; minority carriers drift across the junction
At equilibrium in p-n junction: diffusion current = drift current, establishing the depletion layer and built-in potential

questions.solution: Diffusion current arises due to the concentration gradient of charge carriers. Holes diffuse from the p-side to the n-side and electrons diffuse from the n-side to the p-side; no electric field is required. Drift current, on the other hand, is caused by the electric field that builds up in the depletion region. Minority carriers (electrons on p-side and holes on n-side) drift across the junction under this field. During p-n junction formation, diffusion of majority carriers creates the depletion layer and a built-in electric field. This field opposes further diffusion. At equilibrium, diffusion current equals drift current, and no net current flows.
questions.solution_hindi: विसरण धारा: सांद्रता प्रवणता के कारण होती है (होल p से n की ओर, इलेक्ट्रॉन n से p की ओर)। अपवाह धारा: अवक्षय क्षेत्र के विद्युत-क्षेत्र के कारण होती है। p-n संधि में साम्यावस्था पर विसरण धारा = अपवाह धारा।
questions.topic: p-n junction formation: diffusion and drift currents

questions.text: पट्टिकाओं के बीच 1 mm पृथकन वाले वायु से भरे किसी समान्तर पट्टिका संधारित्र की धारिता 20 pF है। इसे 4·0 μC तक आवेशित किया गया है। यदि पट्टिकाओं पर आवेश समान रहता है, तो पट्टिकाओं के बीच पृथकन 5 mm करने के लिए इसकी पट्टिकाओं को खींचने में किया जाने वाला कार्य परिकलित कीजिए।
questions.text_english: An air-filled parallel plate capacitor with plate separation 1 mm has a capacitance of 20 pF. It is charged to 4·0 μC. Calculate the amount of work done to pull its plates to a separation of 5 mm. Assume the charge on the plates remains the same.

key_points: Initial energy U₁ = Q²/(2C₁) = (4×10⁻⁶)²/(2×20×10⁻¹²) = 0.4 J
New capacitance C₂ = C₁×(d₁/d₂) = 20×(1/5) = 4 pF
Final energy U₂ = Q²/(2C₂) = (4×10⁻⁶)²/(2×4×10⁻¹²) = 2 J; Work done W = U₂ – U₁ = 1.6 J

questions.solution: Initial capacitance C₁ = 20 pF = 20×10⁻¹² F, plate separation d₁ = 1 mm. Charge Q = 4.0 μC = 4×10⁻⁶ C remains constant. Initial energy U₁ = Q²/(2C₁) = (4×10⁻⁶)²/(2×20×10⁻¹²) = 16×10⁻¹²/(40×10⁻¹²) = 0.4 J. New separation d₂ = 5 mm, so new capacitance C₂ = ε₀A/d₂ = C₁×(d₁/d₂) = 20×(1/5) = 4 pF. Final energy U₂ = Q²/(2C₂) = (4×10⁻⁶)²/(2×4×10⁻¹²) = 16×10⁻¹²/(8×10⁻¹²) = 2 J. Work done W = U₂ – U₁ = 2 – 0.4 = 1.6 J.
questions.solution_hindi: U₁ = Q²/(2C₁) = 0.4 J। C₂ = 4 pF। U₂ = Q²/(2C₂) = 2 J। W = U₂ – U₁ = 1.6 J।
questions.topic: Energy stored in a capacitor and work done in changing plate separation

questions.text:
(क) धारा घनत्व परिभाषित कीजिए। क्या यह अदिश है या सदिश ? किसी धातु के चालक में कोई विद्युत-क्षेत्र E बनाए रखा गया है। यदि इस चालक के प्रति एकांक आयतन में इलेक्ट्रॉनों (द्रव्यमान m, आवेश e) की संख्या n है तथा इसका विश्रान्ति काल τ है, तो यह दर्शाए कि धारा घनत्व j = σE है, जहाँ σ = ne²τ/m है।
अथवा
(ख) व्हीटस्टोन सेतु किसे कहते हैं ? व्हीटस्टोन सेतु के संतुलन के लिए आवश्यक शर्तें प्राप्त कीजिए।
questions.text_english:
(a) Define current density. Is it a scalar or a vector? An electric field E is maintained in a metallic conductor. If n be the number of electrons (mass m, charge e) per unit volume in the conductor and τ its relaxation time, show that the current density j = σE, where σ = ne²τ/m.
OR
(b) What is a Wheatstone bridge? Obtain the necessary conditions under which the Wheatstone bridge is balanced.

key_points: (a) Current density j = I/A; it is a vector quantity in the direction of current flow
Drift velocity: vd = eEτ/m; current I = nAevd = nAe(eEτ/m); j = I/A = ne²τE/m = σE
(b) Wheatstone bridge: balanced when P/Q = R/S, i.e., no current through galvanometer

questions.solution:
Part (a): Current density is defined as the current flowing per unit cross-sectional area perpendicular to the direction of flow: j = I/A. It is a vector quantity directed along the conventional current. Under an electric field E, the acceleration of each electron is a = eE/m. The drift velocity is vd = aτ = eEτ/m. Current I = nAevd = nAe(eEτ/m). Therefore j = I/A = ne²τE/m = σE, where σ = ne²τ/m. This is Ohm's law in microscopic form.

Part (b) OR: A Wheatstone bridge consists of four resistances P, Q, R, and S arranged in a diamond shape with a battery across one diagonal and a galvanometer across the other. The bridge is balanced when no current flows through the galvanometer. Applying Kirchhoff's laws at balance: P/Q = R/S. This is the condition for a balanced Wheatstone bridge.
questions.solution_hindi:
(क) धारा घनत्व j = I/A एक सदिश राशि है। अपवाह वेग vd = eEτ/m। j = nevd = ne²τE/m = σE, जहाँ σ = ne²τ/m।
(ख) व्हीटस्टोन सेतु: P/Q = R/S पर संतुलित।
questions.topic: Current density, drift velocity, Ohm's law derivation; Wheatstone bridge

questions.text: अनुप्रस्थ-काट क्षेत्रफल 0·2 cm² की किसी वृत्ताकार कुण्डली से 4 A धारा प्रवाहित हो रही है। इसे 0·5 T परिमाण के एकसमान चुम्बकीय क्षेत्र में इस प्रकार रखा गया है कि कुण्डली का तल चुम्बकीय क्षेत्र के अभिलम्बवत् हो। परिकलित कीजिए : (क) कुण्डली पर नेट बल। (ख) कुण्डली पर बल-आघूर्ण। (ग) इस कुण्डली के प्रत्येक इलेक्ट्रॉन पर चुम्बकीय क्षेत्र के कारण औसत बल। इस कुण्डली के पदार्थ में मुक्त इलेक्ट्रॉन घनत्व 10²⁸ m⁻³ है।
questions.text_english: A circular coil with cross-sectional area 0·2 cm² carries a current of 4 A. It is kept in a uniform magnetic field of magnitude 0·5 T normal to the plane of the coil. Calculate: (a) the net force on the coil. (b) the torque on the coil. (c) the average force on each electron in the coil due to the magnetic field. The free electron density in the material of the coil is 10²⁸ m⁻³.

key_points: (a) Net force on a closed loop in a uniform field = 0
(b) Torque τ = NIA×B×sinθ; plane is normal to B means angle between moment and B is 0°; so τ = 0

questions.solution:
Part (a): In a uniform magnetic field, the net force on any closed current-carrying loop is zero, because the forces on opposite elements cancel out. Net force = 0.

Part (b): Torque τ = NIAB sinθ, where θ is the angle between the magnetic moment (normal to coil plane) and B. Since the plane of the coil is normal to B, the magnetic moment is parallel to B (θ = 0°). Therefore τ = NIAB sin0° = 0.

Part (c): The drift velocity of electrons: I = nAevd, so vd = I/(nAe). Force on each electron: F = evdB = e × [I/(nAe)] × B = IB/(nA). Here n = 10²⁸ m⁻³, A = 0.2 cm² = 0.2×10⁻⁴ m², I = 4 A, B = 0.5 T. F = (4×0.5)/(10²⁸×0.2×10⁻⁴) = 2/(2×10²³) = 10⁻²³ N.
questions.solution_hindi: (क) एकसमान चुम्बकीय क्षेत्र में बन्द पाश पर नेट बल = 0। (ख) कुण्डली का तल B के अभिलम्ब है, अतः τ = 0। (ग) F = IB/(nA) = (4×0.5)/(10²⁸×0.2×10⁻⁴) = 10⁻²³ N।

(ख) क्या किसी श्रेणी LCR परिपथ में किसी प्रेरक अथवा संधारित्र के सिरों पर वोल्टता पात ac स्रोत की अनुप्रयुक्त वोल्टता से अधिक हो सकती है ? अपने उत्तर की पुष्टि कीजिए।
questions.text_english:
(a) Draw the graphs showing the variation of the following with the frequency of ac source in a circuit: (i) Resistance (ii) Capacitive reactance (iii) Inductive reactance
(b) Can the voltage drop across the inductor or the capacitor in a series LCR circuit be greater than the applied voltage of the ac source? Justify your answer.

key_points: (a) R vs f: horizontal straight line (R independent of frequency); Xc vs f: hyperbolic curve decreasing (Xc = 1/2πfC); XL vs f: straight line through origin increasing (XL = 2πfL)
(b) Yes, voltage across L or C can exceed applied voltage in a series LCR circuit
At resonance, VL = IXL and VC = IXC can each be greater than V if Q-factor > 1

questions.solution:
Part (a): Resistance R does not depend on frequency, so its graph is a straight horizontal line parallel to the frequency axis. Capacitive reactance Xc = 1/(2πfC) decreases with increasing frequency, giving a hyperbolic curve. Inductive reactance XL = 2πfL increases linearly with frequency, giving a straight line passing through the origin.

Part (b): Yes, the voltage across the inductor or capacitor in a series LCR circuit can exceed the applied voltage. At resonance, the impedance Z = R (minimum). The current I = V/R. Voltage across inductor VL = IXL = VXL/R = V×Q, where Q = XL/R is the quality factor. If Q > 1, then VL > V. Similarly VC > V. This is known as voltage resonance. The voltages across L and C are equal and opposite at resonance, so they cancel, but individually each can exceed the source voltage.
questions.solution_hindi:
(क) R-f: क्षैतिज रेखा; Xc-f: अतिपरवलयिक (घटता); XL-f: मूल बिंदु से उठती सीधी रेखा।
(ख) हाँ, अनुनाद पर VL = VC = V×Q > V यदि Q > 1।

(क) नाभिक के किन्हीं दो गुणों को लिखिए।
(ख) किसी परमाणु की तुलना में नाभिक का घनत्व बहुत अधिक क्यों होता है ?
(ग) यह दर्शाए कि सभी नाभिकों के लिए नाभिकीय द्रव्य का घनत्व समान होता है।
questions.text_english:
(a) State any two properties of a nucleus.
(b) Why is the density of a nucleus much more than that of an atom?
(c) Show that the density of the nuclear matter is the same for all nuclei.

key_points: (a) Nuclear size R = R₀A^(1/3); nucleus contains protons and neutrons; nuclear forces are short-range and strong
(b) Nuclear radius ~10⁻¹⁵ m vs atomic radius ~10⁻¹⁰ m; almost all mass in nucleus; density = mass/volume enormously larger
(c) ρ = mass/volume = (A×m_p)/(4/3 π R₀³ A) = 3m_p/(4πR₀³) = constant, independent of A

questions.solution:
Part (a): Two properties of a nucleus are: (1) The radius of a nucleus is given by R = R₀A^(1/3), where R₀ ≈ 1.2 fm and A is the mass number, showing that nuclear size increases with mass number. (2) The nucleus is composed of protons and neutrons (nucleons) held together by strong nuclear forces which are short-range and charge-independent.

Part (b): The radius of an atom (~10⁻¹⁰ m) is about 10⁵ times larger than the nuclear radius (~10⁻¹⁵ m). Almost all the mass of an atom is concentrated in its tiny nucleus. Since density = mass/volume, and the volume of the nucleus is enormously smaller than the atom while the mass is nearly the same, the nuclear density is about 10¹⁵ times greater than atomic density.

Part (c): Nuclear density ρ = (mass of nucleus)/(volume of nucleus) = (A × mₚ) / (4/3 π R³) = (A × mₚ) / (4/3 π R₀³ A) = 3mₚ/(4πR₀³). This expression is independent of mass number A, proving that nuclear density is the same for all nuclei.
questions.solution_hindi: (क) R = R₀A^(1/3); नाभिक में प्रोटॉन और न्यूट्रॉन होते हैं। (ख) नाभिकीय त्रिज्या ~10⁻¹⁵ m, परमाणु त्रिज्या ~10⁻¹⁰ m; द्रव्यमान नाभिक में संकेंद्रित। (ग) ρ = 3mₚ/(4πR₀³), A पर निर्भर नहीं, अतः सभी नाभिकों के लिए समान।

questions.text: हाइड्रोजन परमाणु के बोर के सिद्धान्त के तीन अभिगृहीतों का उल्लेख कीजिए। कोई हाइड्रोजन परमाणु स्तर n से स्तर (n–1) को व्युत्तेजित होता है। यह दर्शाए कि बोर के सिद्धान्त के अनुसार, n के बृहत् मानों के लिए उत्सर्जित विकिरण की आवृत्ति ν ∝ n⁻³ होती है, जहाँ ν = स्थिरांक। यह परिणाम ठीक-ठीक मेल खाता है और यह बोर के सिद्धान्त की सफलताओं में से एक है।
questions.text_english: State the three postulates of Bohr's theory of hydrogen atom. A hydrogen atom de-excites from level n to level (n–1). Show that, for large values of n, the frequency of radiation emitted ν ∝ n⁻³, where ν is a constant. This result exactly agrees with that obtained from classical physics and is one of the successes of Bohr's theory.

key_points: Postulate 1: Electrons revolve in stationary orbits without radiating energy
Postulate 2: Angular momentum of electron is quantized: mvr = nh/(2π)
Postulate 3: Radiation is emitted when electron jumps from higher to lower orbit: hν = E_n – E_(n-1); for large n, ν = me⁴/(4ε₀²h³) × (2/n³) ∝ n⁻³

questions.solution:
The three postulates of Bohr's theory are: (1) An electron in an atom revolves in certain stable circular orbits (called stationary states) without emitting radiation. (2) Only those orbits are allowed in which the angular momentum of the electron is an integral multiple of h/2π: mvr = nh/2π. (3) Radiation is emitted (or absorbed) when an electron jumps from a higher energy orbit to a lower one; the energy of the emitted photon is hν = E_high – E_low.

For the transition from n to (n–1): Energy of level n is E_n = –13.6/n² eV. The emitted frequency: hν = E_n–E_(n–1) = 13.6[(1/(n–1)²) – (1/n²)] eV. For large n: (1/(n–1)² – 1/n²) ≈ (n² – (n–1)²)/(n²(n–1)²) ≈ (2n–1)/(n⁴) ≈ 2/n³. Therefore ν = (13.6 × e)/(h) × 2/n³ ∝ n⁻³. This matches the classical result for orbital frequency.
questions.solution_hindi: बोर के तीन अभिगृहीत: (1) स्थायी कक्षाएं - विकिरण नहीं। (2) कोणीय संवेग: mvr = nh/2π। (3) ऊर्जा उत्सर्जन/अवशोषण: hν = E_n – E_(n-1)। n से (n–1) संक्रमण पर बड़े n के लिए ν ∝ n⁻³।

questions.text:
(क) विद्युत-चुम्बकीय तरंग की तरंगदैर्घ्य को प्रायः विकिरण उत्पन्न करने वाले निकाय के अभिलाक्षणिक साइज़ से संबंधित किया जाता है। इस कथन की पुष्टि के लिए दो उदाहरण दीजिए।
(ख) (i) लम्बी दूरियों के रेडियो प्रसारण के लिए लघु-तरंग बैण्ड का उपयोग किया जाता है। क्यों ? (ii) प्रकाशिक और रेडियो दूरबीन (दूरदर्शक) धरती पर स्थापित की जाती हैं, परन्तु X-किरण खगोलिकी केवल पृथ्वी की कक्षा में परिक्रमा करने वाले उपग्रहों से ही सम्भव है। क्यों ?
questions.text_english:
(a) The wavelength of an electromagnetic wave is generally related to the characteristic size of the system that radiates it. Give two examples to justify this statement.
(b) (i) Long distance radio broadcasts use short-wave bands. Why? (ii) Optical and radio telescopes are built on the ground, but X-ray astronomy is possible only from satellites orbiting the Earth. Why?

key_points: (a) Example 1: Atomic transitions (~10⁻¹⁰ m size) emit visible/UV light (~10⁻⁷ m); Example 2: Nuclear transitions (~10⁻¹⁵ m) emit gamma rays (~10⁻¹² m)
(b)(i) Short waves (high frequency) are reflected by the ionosphere and can travel long distances around the Earth's curvature
(b)(ii) Earth's atmosphere absorbs X-rays; satellites above atmosphere allow X-ray astronomy

questions.solution:
Part (a): Example 1 – Atomic transitions involve electrons at distances ~10⁻¹⁰ m (atomic size). The emitted radiation has wavelengths in the visible or UV range (~10⁻⁷ m), of similar order. Example 2 – Nuclear transitions occur within a nucleus of size ~10⁻¹⁵ m, and the emitted gamma rays have wavelengths ~10⁻¹² m, consistent with the nuclear scale.

Part (b)(i): Short waves (frequencies 3–30 MHz) are reflected by the ionosphere back to Earth's surface. This allows them to travel long distances by successive reflections between the ground and ionosphere, making them suitable for long-distance radio broadcasts.

Part (b)(ii): The Earth's atmosphere is opaque to X-rays; it absorbs them completely before they can reach the ground. Therefore, X-ray telescopes must be placed on satellites orbiting above the atmosphere. Optical and radio waves, however, pass through the atmosphere with little absorption, so ground-based optical and radio telescopes work effectively.
questions.solution_hindi: (क) परमाणु (10⁻¹⁰ m) → UV/दृश्य प्रकाश; नाभिक (10⁻¹⁵ m) → गामा किरणें। (ख)(i) लघु तरंगें आयनमण्डल से परावर्तित होती हैं। (ii) वायुमण्डल X-किरणों को अवशोषित करता है।

questions.text: कोई लेंस दो पृष्ठों से घिरा कोई पारदर्शी माध्यम होता है जिसका एक अथवा दोनों पृष्ठ गोलीय होते हैं। किसी लेंस की फोकस दूरी उसके दोनों पृष्ठों की वक्रता त्रिज्याओं और लेंस के पदार्थ के, उस पदार्थ के सापेक्ष जिससे लेंस घिरा है, अपवर्तनांक द्वारा निर्धारित की जाती है। किसी लेंस की क्षमता उसकी फोकस दूरी की व्युत्क्रम होती है। यदि कई लेंसों को संपर्क में रखा जाता है, तो संयोजन की क्षमता उन लेंसों की अपनी-अपनी क्षमताओं का बीजगणितीय योग होता है।
questions.text_english: A lens is a transparent medium bounded by two surfaces, with one or both surfaces being spherical. The focal length of a lens is determined by the radii of curvature of its two surfaces and the refractive index of its medium with respect to that of the surrounding medium. The power of a lens is reciprocal of its focal length. If a number of lenses are kept in contact, the power of the combination is the algebraic sum of the powers of the individual lenses.
questions.instruction_line: निम्नलिखित गद्यांश को पढ़कर प्रश्नों के उत्तर दीजिए।

questions.solution: Passage-based question set. Answers are provided in sub_questions.

sub_questions.text: किसी काँच के बने उभयोत्तल लेंस के दोनों फलकों की वक्रता त्रिज्या R समान है तथा काँच का अपवर्तनांक n है। इस लेंस की क्षमता है :
sub_questions.text_english: A double-convex lens, with each face having same radius of curvature R, is made of glass of refractive index n. Its power is :
sub_questions.solution: For a double-convex lens with equal radii of curvature R, using the lens maker's formula: 1/f = (n–1)[1/R₁ – 1/R₂] = (n–1)[1/R – (–1/R)] = (n–1)(2/R) = 2(n–1)/R. Power P = 1/f = 2(n–1)/R.

sub_questions.text: क्षमता P के किसी उभयोत्तल लेंस, जिसके दोनों फलकों की वक्रता त्रिज्या समान है, को उसके मुख्य अक्ष के लम्बवत् दो समान भागों में काटा गया है। लेंस के एक भाग की क्षमता होगी :
sub_questions.text_english: A double-convex lens of power P, with each face having same radius of curvature, is cut into two equal parts perpendicular to its principal axis. The power of one part of the lens will be :
sub_questions.solution: When a double-convex lens is cut perpendicular to its principal axis, each part becomes a plano-convex lens. For each part, one radius of curvature is R and the other is ∞. Using lens maker's formula: 1/f' = (n–1)(1/R) = half of the original 2(n–1)/R. So P' = P/2 for each part.

sub_questions.text: उपर्युक्त लेंस के दोनों भागों को आरेख में दर्शाए अनुसार एक-दूसरे के संपर्क में रखा गया है। इस संयोजन की क्षमता होगी :
sub_questions.text_english: The above two parts are kept in contact with each other as shown in the figure. The power of the combination will be :
sub_questions.solution: When the two halves (each of power P/2) are placed in contact as shown (forming an X-shape, like the original lens), the combined power = P/2 + P/2 = P. The combination behaves as the original double-convex lens.

sub_questions.text:
(क) क्षमता P के किसी उभयोत्तल लेंस, जिसके दोनों फलकों की वक्रता त्रिज्या समान है, को उसके मुख्य अक्ष के अनुदिश दो भागों में काटकर दोनों भागों को आरेख में दर्शाए अनुसार व्यवस्थित किया गया है। इस संयोजन की क्षमता होगी :
अथवा
(ख) 60 cm और 20 cm फोकस दूरी के दो उत्तल लेंसों को एक-दूसरे के संपर्क में समाक्षतः रखा गया है। इस संयोजन की क्षमता है :
sub_questions.text_english:
(a) A double-convex lens of power P, with each face having same radius of curvature, is cut along its principal axis. The two parts are arranged as shown in the figure. The power of the combination will be :
OR
(b) Two convex lenses of focal lengths 60 cm and 20 cm are held coaxially in contact with each other. The power of the combination is :
sub_questions.solution:
Part (a): When a double-convex lens is cut along the principal axis, each half is a plano-convex lens of power P/2. When arranged as shown (flat faces facing each other, creating a shape where the curved surfaces face outward), one acts as a converging lens and the other as a diverging lens of equal power P/2. Combined power = P/2 + (–P/2) = 0 (Zero).

Part (b) OR: For two lenses in contact, combined power P = P₁ + P₂ = 1/f₁ + 1/f₂ = 1/0.60 + 1/0.20 = 5/3 + 5 = 1.67 + 5 = 6.67 D ≈ 6.6 D.

questions.text: संधि डायोड दिष्टकारी के रूप में: ac वोल्टता को dc वोल्टता में परिवर्तित करने की प्रक्रिया को दिष्टकरण कहते हैं और इस परिवर्तन को सम्पन्न करने वाली युक्ति को दिष्टकारी कहते हैं। किसी p-n संधि डायोड के अभिलाक्षणिकों से यह ज्ञात होता है कि जब p-n संधि डायोड अग्रदिशिक बायसित होता है, तो उसका प्रतिरोध निम्न होता है तथा जब पश्चदिशिक बायसित होता है, तो उसका प्रतिरोध उच्च होता है। p-n संधि डायोड केवल अग्रदिशिक बायस होने पर ही चालन करता है। p-n संधि डायोड का यही गुण दिष्टकारी के रूप में इसके उपयोग के लिए इसे उपयुक्त बनाता है। इस प्रकार, जब किसी ac वोल्टता को किसी p-n संधि के सिरों पर अनुप्रयुक्त किया जाता है, तो यह केवल उन्हीं प्रत्यावर्ती अर्ध-चक्रों में चालन करती है जब यह अग्रदिशिक बायस होती है। वह दिष्टकारी जो किसी ac वोल्टता के अर्ध-चक्र का दिष्टकरण करता है, उसे अर्ध-तरंग दिष्टकारी कहते हैं और जो दोनों अर्ध-चक्रों का दिष्टकरण करता है, उसे पूर्ण-तरंग दिष्टकारी कहते हैं।
questions.text_english: Junction Diode as a Rectifier: The process of conversion of an ac voltage into a dc voltage is called rectification and the device which performs this conversion is called a rectifier. The characteristics of a p-n junction diode reveal that when a p-n junction diode is forward biased, it offers a low resistance and when it is reverse biased, it offers a high resistance. Hence, a p-n junction diode conducts only when it is forward biased. This property of a p-n junction diode makes it suitable for its use as a rectifier. Thus, when an ac voltage is applied across a p-n junction, it conducts only during those alternate half cycles for which it is forward biased. A rectifier which rectifies only half cycle of an ac voltage is called a half-wave rectifier and one that rectifies both the half cycles is known as a full-wave rectifier.

questions.text_english:
(a) (i) A resistor and a capacitor are connected in series to an ac source v = vm sin ωt. Derive an expression for the impedance of the circuit.
(ii) When does an inductor act as a conductor in a circuit? Give reason for it.
(iii) An electric lamp is designed to operate at 110 V dc and 11 A current. If the lamp is operated on 220 V, 50 Hz ac source with a coil in series, then find the inductance of the coil.
OR
(b) (i) Draw a labelled diagram of a step-up transformer and describe its working principle. Explain any three causes for energy losses in a real transformer.
(ii) A step-up transformer converts a low voltage into high voltage. Does it violate the principle of conservation of energy? Explain.
(iii) A step-up transformer has 200 and 3000 turns in its primary and secondary coils respectively. The input voltage given to the primary coil is 90 V. Calculate: (1) The output voltage across the secondary coil. (2) The current in the primary coil if the current in the secondary coil is 2·0 A.

key_points: (a)(i) Z = √(R² + Xc²) = √(R² + 1/(ω²C²)); phasor diagram gives V² = VR² + VC²
(a)(ii) Inductor acts as a conductor at very high frequency (XL = ωL → ∞) No — at DC (ω=0) XL=0 acts as pure conductor; at high freq it resists
(a)(iii) Lamp resistance R = 110/11 = 10 Ω; for same current with 220V: Z = 220/11 = 20 Ω; XL = √(Z²–R²) = √(400–100) = √300; L = XL/(2πf) ≈ 0.55 H

questions.solution:
Part (a)(i): For a series RC circuit with v = vm sinωt, the voltage across resistor is VR = IR and across capacitor VC = IXC = I/(ωC). Using phasor diagram, VR is in phase with I and VC lags I by 90°. The applied voltage V = √(VR² + VC²). Impedance Z = V/I = √(R² + (1/ωC)²).

Part (a)(ii): An inductor acts as a pure conductor (wire) when direct current (dc) or very low frequency ac flows through it. At ω = 0 (dc), the inductive reactance XL = ωL = 0, so it offers no opposition to current flow and behaves like a simple conducting wire.

Part (a)(iii): Lamp resistance R = V/I = 110/11 = 10 Ω. For the lamp to carry the same current of 11 A with 220 V ac supply, total impedance Z = 220/11 = 20 Ω. Inductive reactance XL = √(Z² – R²) = √(400 – 100) = √300 = 10√3 Ω. Inductance L = XL/(2πf) = 10√3/(2π×50) = 10×1.732/314.16 ≈ 0.055 H.

Part (b)(i) OR: A step-up transformer has more turns in the secondary coil than in the primary. When alternating current flows in the primary, it creates a changing magnetic flux in the iron core. This changing flux induces an emf in the secondary coil by mutual induction. The ratio Vs/Vp = Ns/Np > 1, so secondary voltage is higher. Energy losses in a real transformer: (1) Copper loss — heat generated in resistance of windings (I²R); minimized by using thick low-resistance wire. (2) Iron/Core loss — eddy currents in the iron core generate heat; minimized by using laminated core. (3) Hysteresis loss — energy needed to magnetize and demagnetize the core each cycle; minimized by using soft iron core with low hysteresis.

Part (b)(ii): A step-up transformer does not violate energy conservation. Although voltage increases, current decreases proportionally (Vs/Vp = Ip/Is). The power output (VsIs) equals power input (VpIp) in an ideal transformer. In practice, output power is slightly less due to energy losses, but no extra energy is created.

Part (b)(iii): (1) Vs = (Ns/Np) × Vp = (3000/200) × 90 = 15 × 90 = 1350 V. (2) For an ideal transformer, VpIp = VsIs, so Ip = (Vs/Vp) × Is = (1350/90) × 2.0 = 15 × 2.0 = 30 A.
questions.solution_hindi: (क)(i) Z = √(R² + 1/ω²C²)। (ii) dc पर XL = 0, प्रेरक चालक की तरह। (iii) L ≈ 0.055 H। (ख)(i) स्टेप-अप ट्रांसफॉर्मर का सिद्धान्त: अन्योन्य प्रेरण। ऊर्जा हृास: ताम्र हानि, लोह हानि, शैथिल्य हानि। (ii) ऊर्जा संरक्षण का उल्लंघन नहीं: Ip/Is = Vs/Vp। (iii) Vs = 1350 V; Ip = 30 A।

(a) (i) Derive an expression for potential energy of an electric dipole p in an external uniform electric field E. When is the potential energy of the dipole (1) maximum, and (2) minimum?
(ii) An electric dipole consists of point charges –1·0 pC and +1·0 pC located at (0, 0) and (3 mm, 4 mm) respectively in x–y plane. An electric field E = 1000 V/m î is switched on in the region. Find the torque acting on the dipole.
OR
(b) (i) An electric dipole (dipole moment p = pî), consisting of charges –q and +q, separated by distance 2a, is placed along the x-axis, with its centre at the origin. Show that the potential V, due to this dipole, at a point x (x >> a) is equal to (1/4πε₀)(p/x²).
(ii) Two isolated metallic spheres S₁ and S₂ of radii 1 cm and 3 cm respectively are charged such that both have the same charge density 9×10⁻² C/m². They are placed far away from each other and connected by a thin wire. Calculate the new charge on sphere S₁.

key_points: (a)(i) U = –pE cosθ; max at θ=180° (U=+pE); min at θ=0° (U=–pE)
(a)(ii) Dipole length = √((3mm)²+(4mm)²) = 5mm; p = q×d = 1pC×5mm = 5×10⁻¹⁵ C·m; τ = pE sinθ where angle of p with E; p along (3,4)/5 so sinθ = 4/5; τ = 5×10⁻¹⁵×1000×(4/5) = 4×10⁻¹²
(b)(ii) Q₁ = σ×4πR₁²; Q₂ = σ×4πR₂²; total Q = σ×4π(R₁²+R₂²); after connection, same potential; new Q₁' = Q_total×R₁/(R₁+R₂)

questions.solution:
Part (a)(i): The work done to rotate a dipole from angle 0° to θ in a uniform electric field E is W = pE(1 – cosθ). Taking the reference at θ = 90°, potential energy U = –pE cosθ. Potential energy is maximum (U = +pE) when θ = 180° (dipole antiparallel to E) and minimum (U = –pE) when θ = 0° (dipole parallel to E, stable equilibrium).

Part (a)(ii): The dipole vector goes from –q at (0,0) to +q at (3mm, 4mm). Length = √(9+16) mm = 5 mm = 5×10⁻³ m. Dipole moment magnitude p = q×d = 1×10⁻¹² × 5×10⁻³ = 5×10⁻¹⁵ C·m. Direction of p: unit vector = (3î + 4ĵ)/5. The electric field E = 1000î V/m. Torque τ = p→ × E→ = (5×10⁻¹⁵)(3î+4ĵ)/5 × 1000î = 10⁻¹⁵(3î+4ĵ) × 1000î = 10⁻¹² [3(î×î) + 4(ĵ×î)] = 10⁻¹² [0 + 4(–k̂)] = –4×10⁻¹² k̂ N·m. Magnitude of torque = 4×10⁻¹² N·m.

Part (b)(i) OR: Potential at point P(x, 0) on the axial line: V = (1/4πε₀)[q/(x–a) + (–q)/(x+a)] = (q/4πε₀)[(x+a–x+a)/((x–a)(x+a))] = (q/4πε₀)(2a/(x²–a²)). For x >> a: x²–a² ≈ x². So V = (1/4πε₀)(2qa/x²) = (1/4πε₀)(p/x²), where p = 2qa. Hence proved.

Part (b)(ii): Initial charges: Q₁ = σ×4πR₁² = 9×10⁻²×4π×(0.01)² = 9×10⁻²×4π×10⁻⁴ = 36π×10⁻⁶ C. Q₂ = σ×4πR₂² = 9×10⁻²×4π×(0.03)² = 9×10⁻²×4π×9×10⁻⁴ = 324π×10⁻⁶ C. Total charge Q = 360π×10⁻⁶ C. When connected, they reach the same potential: V = Q₁'/R₁ = Q₂'/R₂, so Q₁'/Q₂' = R₁/R₂ = 1/3. Also Q₁' + Q₂' = Q_total = 360π×10⁻⁶. Therefore Q₁' = (1/4)×360π×10⁻⁶ = 90π×10⁻⁶ C ≈ 2.83×10⁻⁴ C.

Find the value of λ.

key_points: (a)(i) Graph: U-shaped curve with minimum at angle of minimum deviation δm; define δm as the minimum value of deviation angle
(a)(ii) Normal incidence means i₁=0 so r₁=0; all deviation occurs at second surface; r₂=A; n = sinA+δ)/sinA follows from Snell's law at second surface

questions.solution:
Part (a)(i): As the angle of incidence increases from 0°, the angle of deviation first decreases, reaches a minimum value (called the angle of minimum deviation δm), and then increases again. The graph is a U-shaped curve. The angle of minimum deviation δm is defined as the minimum value of the angle of deviation suffered by a ray while passing through a prism.

Part (a)(ii): When a ray is incident normally on the first refracting face, angle of incidence i₁ = 0°, so angle of refraction r₁ = 0°. The ray travels undeviated to the second face. At the second face, the angle of incidence r₂ = A (prism angle). The total deviation δ = r₂ – (angle at exit). Applying Snell's law at second surface: n×sinA = 1×sin(A+δ), giving n = sin(A+δ)/sinA.

Part (a)(iii): n = √2, A = 60°. At minimum deviation: n = sin((A+δm)/2) / sin(A/2). √2 = sin((60°+δm)/2) / sin30° = sin((60°+δm)/2) / 0.5. So sin((60°+δm)/2) = √2 × 0.5 = 1/√2. Therefore (60°+δm)/2 = 45°, giving 60° + δm = 90°, so δm = 30°. Angle of incidence i = (A+δm)/2 = (60°+30°)/2 = 45°.

Part (b)(i) OR: Huygens' principle states that every point on a wavefront acts as a source of secondary wavelets, and the new wavefront at any later time is the common tangential surface (envelope) of all these secondary wavelets. For reflection: draw incident wavefront AB making angle i with mirror. Point A touches mirror at time t=0 and draws a secondary wavelet of radius ct (where c is wave speed) by the time the other end B reaches B'. Draw tangent from B' to this sphere — this tangent B'A' is the reflected wavefront. Using geometry: triangles ABB' and A'B'A are congruent (AB' = AB', right angles equal, hypotenuse common), so angle of reflection = angle of incidence.

Part (b)(ii): Coherent sources are those that emit light of the same frequency and have a constant phase difference between them. Two independent sodium lamps cannot act as coherent sources because they are independent — their phase difference changes randomly over time due to different emission processes. Coherent sources are typically produced from a single source (like in Young's experiment, one source is split into two by a double slit).

Part (b)(iii): For the nth bright fringe in Young's double slit experiment, position yn = nλD/d. For the fourth bright fringe of unknown λ to coincide with the fifth bright fringe of known λ (520 nm): 4λD/d = 5×520×D/d. Therefore 4λ = 5×520 = 2600, giving λ = 2600/4 = 650 nm.
